metaDescription: Six battery and rechargeable LED puck lights compared on lumens, colour temperature, remotes, motion sensors and mounting, with honest notes on adhesive.
expertTake: The EZVALO rechargeable puck set with three colour temperatures is the best overall pick because it removes disposable batteries and offers a proper white range. The Amazon Basics puck is the value pick for a single dark shelf. Skip the category if you want even task light along a countertop, because pucks make pools of light and a linear bar does that job better.
introParagraphs: A puck light is a small round LED, usually battery powered, that you stick or screw under a shelf, inside a closet or on a cabinet to light a dark spot without any wiring. They are popular with renters and for places where an outlet is out of reach.

They are simple devices, and the differences come down to brightness, colour temperature, how they are powered and how they stick. This guide compares six sets and explains the limits of a small light so that you buy for the right job.

products.name: EZVALO rechargeable puck lights with 3 colour temperatures, RGB and IR remote
products.description:
This EZVALO set uses rechargeable 800mAh cells instead of disposable AAA batteries, and offers three white colour temperatures plus 16 RGB colours. You can tap each puck for quick changes or use the IR remote for colours, timer and modes. Rechargeable cells mean no stream of spent batteries.

The tradeoff is that charging means taking each puck down, and 800mAh runs a small LED for limited hours, particularly at higher brightness. Compared with the Amazon Basics puck, it costs more and offers far more control, but the basic function is the same. A puck is still a spot light, not a bar.

In ownership terms, charge the pucks in batches and set the white temperature to match your room, typically warm white for a kitchen or closet. Use the adhesive on clean, dry surfaces, and avoid greasy zones near a cooktop. It suits closets, pantry shelves and display cabinets. When you place the pucks, set them toward the front edge of the shelf so the light falls on the items and not on the back wall, and stagger them so that the pools of light overlap by a few inches. Rechargeable pucks are easier to live with if you keep a charging routine, such as every second Sunday.
products.bestFor: Closets, pantries and display cabinets where rechargeable pucks with warm white are wanted.
pros: Rechargeable 800mAh cells avoid disposable batteries
Three white temperatures give useful task and ambient light
Tap and remote controls suit different uses
16 RGB colours for accent displays
cons: Charging means removing each puck periodically
A spot light does not give even light along a counter

products.name: Amazon Basics 50 lumen battery operated LED puck lights, push on and off

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Push the lens to switch on or off

products.description:
The Amazon Basics puck delivers 50 lumens and switches on and off when you press the lens, with no switch hardware. It can be mounted with screws or with the double-sided tape that is included, which gives a sturdy hold on a smooth surface. It is the lowest cost tier of the six and a straightforward light.

The tradeoff is the lack of colour options, a remote or a timer, and the dependence on disposable batteries. Compared with the EZVALO rechargeable set, it is simpler and cheaper but more wasteful over time. At 50 lumens it lights a small shelf or a drawer well, but not a long counter.

In ownership terms, fit fresh batteries of one type, mount on a clean dry surface and test the position before pressing the adhesive down. Use screws in a garage or a place that sees vibration. It suits a utility shelf, a toolbox shelf or a closet. Because a push-lens puck is switched by pressure, it can also be knocked on by items stored against it, so leave a small gap around the lens. In a cold garage, alkaline batteries lose capacity, so a lithium AAA cell is a better match if you want reliable winter light.
products.bestFor: Single dark spots such as closets, garages and utility shelves.
pros: Push-lens control needs no switch or remote

products.name: STAR-SPANGLED 2.8 in LED puck lights, 5 pack warm white, Ra 90, battery operated
products.description:
The STAR-SPANGLED set offers five 2.8 in pucks with warm white light and a stated colour rendering index of Ra 90, which means colours appear more natural than under a cheap LED. Each puck uses three AAA batteries, which are not included, and switches on with a press on the lens. The listing describes 0.5 W LEDs at 140 lumens per watt.

The tradeoff is the cost of batteries and the lack of remote control or colour options. Compared with the Amazon Basics puck, a higher CRI gives better colour for fabrics and food, which matters in a pantry or a wardrobe. A warm white fixed light also suits living rooms.

In ownership terms, buy a pack of good AAA batteries, use the adhesive on a clean surface and remove the puck gently when changing batteries. It suits a wardrobe, a shelf or a book nook where colour accuracy matters. Colour rendering matters most when you pick between a navy and a black sweater, or judge whether food has gone off in a pantry, and a light that renders reds and browns properly makes those choices easier. The same quality makes displayed pottery, books and plants look better.
products.bestFor: Wardrobes, pantries and shelves where natural colour rendering matters.
pros: Ra 90 LEDs give more natural colour than basic pucks
Five pucks in a pack cover several shelves
Warm white suits living rooms and bedrooms
Simple press-lens control
cons: Needs 15 AAA batteries across five pucks

products.name: EZVALO RGB under cabinet puck lights, 6-pack with remote, motion sensor, rechargeable
products.description:
This set of six rechargeable pucks includes a motion sensor with a 120 degree detection range, so each light comes on when you step up to the cabinet. You can also use steady-on mode. A remote lets you set brightness, choose white or RGB and use a timed stay-on function with memory.

The tradeoff is that motion sensors can switch on at unwanted times, and a rechargeable battery will not last as long if motion is frequent. Compared with the other EZVALO set, it adds motion but is aimed at hands-free use. A puck with motion is ideal for a closet or a dark hallway shelf.

In ownership terms, aim the sensor toward where you walk, set the stay-on time to suit the task and recharge the pucks when the light dims. It suits closets, stairs, pantries and bathroom cabinets. Point the sensor at the doorway rather than at the shelf, so it wakes as you arrive and not as you pass, and keep it clear of heating vents and curtains that move in drafts. Check how long the light stays on after the last movement, because a short stay-on time can switch off while you are still choosing clothes.
products.bestFor: Closets and pantries where lights should come on without a touch.

Six pucks cover several shelves or cabinets
Remote sets brightness, colour and timer
Rechargeable, so no disposable batteries
cons: Motion triggers can run the battery down in busy areas

products.name: TECOMLIGHT 6-pack puck lights with remote, 3 white tones and 13 colours, AA powered
products.description:
The TECOMLIGHT set includes six pucks with a remote, three white tones and 13 RGB colours, powered by AA batteries. The white tones let you pick warm, natural or cool light for daily tasks, and the colours suit accent lighting. No wiring is needed, and the mounting options include removable adhesive.

The tradeoff is that AA batteries are bulkier than AAA and can be costly over time. Compared with the EZVALO sets, it is battery powered but offers a similar range of modes. Running 18 AA cells is a real cost for six pucks.

In ownership terms, mount the pucks on smooth, clean, dry surfaces, and keep spare batteries. Choose the warm white for living spaces and the cool white for a workshop. It suits a bar, a display or a kitchen shelf where mood and task lighting both matter. Memory functions that restore the last colour are a small convenience, and the six-pack size means you can run a row along a shelf for a continuous wash. Count the battery cost over a year before committing, because six pucks swallow a lot of cells.
products.bestFor: Shelves and displays where both white task light and colour accents are wanted.

products.name: BLS LED puck lights with remote, 6 pucks, 13 colours, 40 lumens max, timer
products.description:
The BLS kit has six pucks and two remotes, with 13 colour options, dimming up to 40 lumens and a timer that shuts the lights off after 30 or 60 minutes. You can use the remote or tap the lens. The two remotes mean one can live in a drawer and one by the sofa.

The tradeoff is brightness: 40 lumens is the lowest in this lineup, so it suits accent and closet use more than task work. Compared with the Amazon Basics puck at 50 lumens, it is dimmer but has more features. Colour lighting with a timer is a good fit for a display shelf or a child's room.

In ownership terms, use the timer so that the lights do not drain the batteries overnight, and mount them at least a couple of inches from a heat source. It suits a bookshelf, a closet or a display where mood matters.
products.bestFor: Display shelves and kids' rooms that want a remote, colours and an auto-off timer.

Timer turns the lights off after 30 or 60 minutes
13 colour options for display lighting
Six pucks cover several shelves
cons: 40 lumens is the dimmest of the six sets

buyingCriteria.explanation: Most battery pucks put out about 40 to 50 lumens, which lights a small shelf or drawer well, but is dim for a countertop task. One puck per 8 to 12 in of cabinet gives even coverage. A common mistake is expecting a few pucks to replace a bar light. Check the lumens on the listing, such as 50 lumens for the Amazon Basics and 40 lumens max for the BLS kit.

Warm white at about 2700K to 3000K is flattering in a living area, while neutral and cool whites suit task work. A high colour rendering index, such as the Ra 90 in the STAR-SPANGLED, makes fabric and food look natural. RGB colours are for accent lighting and do not help vision.

Disposable AAA and AA pucks are cheap to buy but costly to run, while rechargeable pucks such as the EZVALO sets avoid spent batteries. A rechargeable 800mAh cell lasts limited hours at higher brightness. Match power to use: rarely used closets suit batteries, daily-use shelves suit rechargeables.

A press-lens control needs no remote, a remote can control many pucks at once and a motion sensor switches on hands-free. Motion sensors save power but can trigger unnecessarily. A timer prevents all-night use. Choose the control that suits the location. Infrared remotes need a line of sight to each puck, so a remote that works across the room may fail around a corner or through a cabinet door. If you have glass doors on a cabinet, test the remote from where you will stand before you mount every puck.

Most pucks stick on with adhesive tape, which holds well on clean, dry, smooth surfaces and poorly on greasy or textured ones. Screws are the secure option for garages and heavy-use spots. Test the position before pressing the tape, because removal can mark painted surfaces. Wipe the spot with rubbing alcohol first, let it dry fully, and press the puck for about thirty seconds. Adhesive bonds improve over a day, so do not stress the puck by changing batteries immediately after mounting.

Sets range from one to twelve pucks. Count the shelves or cabinets you want to light and buy one extra. White and black housings blend with cabinets. Check the diameter, around 2.8 to 3 in, for the gap under the shelf.

maintenance.why: Weak batteries dim the light. Replace all cells in a puck at once.
Dust and cooking film reduce brightness. A dry or slightly damp cloth works.
Tape loses grip in heat and humidity. Press it back or use screws.
Remote batteries die. Replace them with the right cell.
Leaking cells can corrode contacts. Store pucks without batteries.

faq.q: Are puck lights bright enough for a kitchen counter?
faq.a: Not usually. Battery pucks give about 40 to 50 lumens, which suits shelves and drawers. A counter needs a linear light bar or hardwired lights.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: It depends on brightness and use. Small cells last hours of continuous use, so use a timer or rechargeable set.

faq.q: Will the adhesive damage my cabinets?
faq.a: It can lift paint or finish when removed. Test in a hidden spot, and use screws where a strong hold is needed.
Warm white at 2700K to 3000K suits living areas. Neutral white suits tasks and workshops.
Not for one or two pucks. A remote helps when you have a set of six and want to control all of them at once.

faq.q: Can I use puck lights in a bathroom?
faq.a: Only if the maker says they are suitable for damp places. Keep them away from direct water.
